question: Can one model detect, segment and track every instance of an open-vocabulary visual concept (short noun phrase, image exemplars, or both) in images and videos, and what data and architecture does that take?
hypothesis: Decoupling recognition from localization with a presence head, and training on a large, diverse data-engine dataset with hard negatives and AI verifiers, gives a step change in promptable concept segmentation over existing open-vocabulary detectors.
contributions: introducing the PCS task and SA-Co benchmark
an architecture that decouples recognition, localization and tracking and extends SAM 2 to solve concept segmentation while retaining visual segmentation capabilities
a high-quality, efficient data engine that leverages the complimentary strengths of human and AI annotators

method.summary: SAM 3 is a ~850M-parameter model: a shared Perception Encoder backbone feeds a DETR-style detector (fusion encoder, 6-layer decoder, 200 object queries, global presence token, MaskFormer-style mask head) conditioned on noun-phrase text and image exemplars, plus a SAM 2-style memory tracker for video. It is trained in four stages on SA-Co data built by a human + AI-verifier data engine (Llama 3.2 fine-tuned as mask and exhaustivity verifiers), and evaluated on a new benchmark with the cgF1 metric.
method.task: Promptable Concept Segmentation (open-vocabulary instance/semantic segmentation and video tracking from noun phrases and image exemplars); also Promptable Visual Segmentation (SAM 2 task)

models.name: SAM 3
models.params: ~850M (~450M vision encoder, ~300M text encoder, ~100M detector and tracker)
models.architecture: Shared Perception Encoder; DETR-style detector (fusion encoder of 6 blocks, decoder of 6 blocks, Q=200 object queries, presence token, 4 geometric queries, MaskFormer-style segmentation head, ambiguity head) plus SAM 2-style memory tracker
models.init_from: Perception Encoder (L+ size) pre-trained on 5.4B image-text pairs, no distillation and no video fine-tuning
models.layers: vision encoder 32 layers, 4 with global attention; fusion encoder 6; decoder 6
models.context: text encoder is causal, max context length 32

other.input_resolution: 1008 x 1008, PE patch size 14 (inferred from 'PE-L+ (14)' in Table 11)
other.attention: windowed 24x24 tokens except global layers; image of 1008 px split into 3x3 windows of 336 px
other.token_downsampling: 2x2 to 1296 tokens before the fusion encoder (ablation setup)
other.ambiguity_head: mixture of experts, K=2 best, K>3 mode collapse, winner-takes-all
other.latency: 30 ms per image with 100+ objects on an H200; video cost grows linearly with tracked objects

models.name: OWLv2 / OWLv2*
models.architecture: open-vocabulary detector; boxes converted to masks with SAM 1

other.checkpoints: google/owlv2-large-patch14 and google/owlv2-large-patch14-ensemble; * is partially trained on LVIS

models.name: GroundingDino (gDino-T, gDino-B), LLMDet (L, B), APE-D, DINO-X, Gemini 2.5 Flash/Pro, T-Rex2, GLEE, Molmo-72B, Qwen2-VL-72B

other.detection_thresholds: swept at 0.1 steps on LVIS cgF1: 0.4 for LLMDet-L, LLMDet-B, gDino-T; 0.3 for OWLv2*; 0.2 for OWLv2 and gDino-B; 0.5 for DINO-X

models.name: Llama 3.2 (fine-tuned as MV and EV AI verifiers)

other.training_data: over 200M image-text pairs to pre-train a foundational verifier, then ~10M high-quality human-annotated points per task

models.name: SAM 3 Agent MLLMs (Qwen2.5-VL 7B/72B, Llama4 Maverick, Qwen3-VL 8B/235B Thinking, Gemini 2.5 Pro)

training.objective: DETR-style set prediction: box L1 weight 5 and gIoU weight 2, classification weight 100, focal 200, dice 10; Align loss in place of IoU prediction loss; DAC-DETR dual supervision; presence BCE weight 20 (stage 3); tracker stage: focal+dice for masks, MAE for IoU, CE for occlusion, weights 20:1:1:1
training.lr: stage 2: initial 5e-4 (1e-4 for vision and text encoder, 1e-3 for all other components); stage 3: all lrs x0.025; stage 4: peak 5.0e-4; long-context tracker fine-tune: x0.1
training.lr_schedule: stage 2: reciprocal square-root with layer-wise lr decay 0.9 on the vision encoder; stage 4: cosine
training.warmup: stage 2: 5k warm-up and cooldown steps; stage 4: linear warmup 1k iterations
training.steps: stage 2: ~95k iterations; stage 3: ~5k iterations; stage 4: ~190k iterations, then 60k iterations on 16- and 32-frame videos
training.regularisation: layer-wise lr decay 0.9; mosaic augmentation up to 3x3; random crop/resize with padding spread over all sides; random horizontal flips; ontology-based synonym and negative sampling; safety negatives (slurs, subjective person adjectives)
training.compute: 172k A100 GPU hours and 86k H200 GPU hours; 142k-176k kWh; 65.3-77.6 metric tons CO2e

other.stage_1: Perception Encoder pre-training, 5.4B image-text pairs, L+ size, vision 450M and text 300M
other.stage_2: detector pre-training on pseudo-labelled and human data; p=0.2 of image-NPs converted to visual queries and p=0.2 augmented with input boxes; PVS interactivity steps capped at 4
other.stage_3: highest-quality exhaustivity-verified data only (SA-Co/SYN dropped), presence token introduced, PVS interactivity 7 steps, PCS interactivity 5 iterations of exemplar boxes
other.few_shot_finetune: 40 epochs, lr one-tenth of standard, batch size 2, mask losses disabled; ODinW13 averaged over three official few-shot splits
other.ablation_setup: stride-28 variant (4x fewer detector tokens), 45% of SA-Co/SYN, shorter schedules, no presence post-training, internal SA-Co/Gold (human cgF1 70.8 vs public 72.8); encoder ablation trained on SA-Co/HQ viewing 5 million samples
other.ambiguity_head: trained on top of a frozen SAM 3

inference.decoding: predictions with confidence above 0.5 are evaluated; scores are the product of presence score and object score
inference.samples: SAM 3 prompted with one NP at a time; ODinW13 few-shot mean and std over three splits; no other seeds or run counts stated
inference.prompting: short noun phrase, image exemplars as positive/negative boxes, or both; video NP prompts global to all frames

parameters.periodic_reprompt_every_N_frames: 16, requires IoU >= 0.8 and detection and masklet scores > 0.8
parameters.counting_postprocessing: no presence token, NMS with IoM threshold 0.5, keep confidence > 0.5, count masks
parameters.video_realtime_parallelism: 30 FPS: up to 10 objects on 2 H200s, 28 on 4, 64 on 8
parameters.mllm_tools: segment_phrase, examine_each_mask, select_masks_and_return, report_no_mask; context pruning back to last segment_phrase call; up to ~60 steps on hard queries

metrics.name: pmF1
metrics.definition: positive micro F1 averaged over IoU thresholds 0.5 to 0.95 step 0.05, on positive media-phrase pairs with at least one ground-truth mask

metrics.name: IL_MCC
metrics.definition: image-level Matthews correlation coefficient of 'is the object present' (any mask with confidence > 0.5), range [-1, 1]

metrics.name: oracle protocol
metrics.definition: prediction compared with each of 3 ground truths, best local F1 selected

metrics.name: pHOTA, pDetA, pAssA, VL_MCC
metrics.definition: HOTA on remapped video-NP pairs (each video-NP its own video id) via TrackEval; video cgF1 = VL_MCC x positive macro F1 with volume IoU

metrics.name: AP, mIoU, J&F, MAE, accuracy, gIoU
metrics.definition: official metric of each public benchmark; LVIS uses AP-fixed

eval.protocol: Single reported number per cell, no confidence intervals or seeds for the main tables; human performance estimated from three annotators (Oracle) and a Random Pair protocol (median of 1000 draws); negatives only have one label so human IL_MCC extrapolated from ~1000 extra annotated image-NPs per domain; ablations use a lighter model and are not comparable across tables.

prompts.text: You are an expert annotator of object segmentation masks. For an image and a pre-deﬁned label, you are given a mask and asked to evaluate the quality of the mask. Follow the following rules when rating the mask. 1. Rate the mask as “Accept” when the label accurately describes the masked object and the mask covers the object with good boundaries. We do not need masks to be pixel-perfect for this task. However, the mask should cover all important parts of the object.

prompts.text: You are an expert annotator of object detection. For an image and a pre-deﬁned label, you are given some boxes and asked to evaluate if the boxes are exhaustive. Follow the following rules when rating the boxes. 1. Rate the boxes as “Accept” when there are no undetected objects that match the label or the label is vague (i.e, “rent”, “it”) or malformed (heavily misspelled). 2. Rate the boxes as “Reject” when there are undetected objects and at least some undetected instances can be separated.
prompts.where: Appendix D.4, Table 22 (first two rules only; remaining rules in the paper)

limits: SAM 3 struggles to generalize to fine-grained out-of-domain concepts (e.g., aircraft types, medical terms) zero-shot, especially in niche domains such as thermal imagery; it adapts with fine-tuning or synthetic domain data (Section B).
Prompts are limited to simple noun phrases; multi-attribute queries beyond one or two attributes and referring expressions are unsupported without an MLLM (SAM 3 Agent).
Video inference cost scales linearly with the number of tracked objects; real-time needs multi-GPU parallelism (10 objects on 2 H200s, 28 on 4, 64 on 8); no shared object-level memory across objects.
A hard 'mode-switch' separates concept prompting from instance (PVS) prompting; interleaving is future work.

The PCS task is intrinsically ambiguous; SA-Co/Gold human cgF1 is 72.8 (oracle) and lower under random pairs (55.5), and the benchmark has one label per hard negative, so human IL_MCC is extrapolated.
Ablations use lighter models and shorter schedules and numbers are not comparable across tables (stated under Table 9).

Many baselines are tuned by the authors (detection thresholds swept on LVIS cgF1; GroundingDino and LLMDet prompted with 20-30 NPs at once); GLEE and LLMDet are zero-shot on SA-Co/VEval and the SmartGlasses egocentric data may lie outside their training distribution.
SAM 3 underperforms Grounding DINO zero-shot on Roboflow100-VL (15.2 vs 15.7 AP); authors attribute it to dataset-specific prompts outside current scope.
SAM 3 Agent on RefCOCO is weaker than trained methods; authors attribute low-IoU cases to annotation bias and ground-truth errors in RefCOCO-Seg (a hypothesis, error analysis in Fig. 28).
No seeds, confidence intervals or run counts are reported for main results; training precision and exact wall-clock are not stated.
Annotation pool does not represent all communities that will use SAM 3 (APAC and EMEA vendors, per the data annotation card); the benchmark is not meant for training.
Models and baselines (Gemini 2.5, Qwen2.5-VL, DINO-X, OWLv2) reflect mid-2025 state of the art and have likely dated.

terms.definition: given an image or short video (<=30 secs), detect, segment and track all instances of a visual concept specified by a short text phrase, image exemplars, or a combination of both
the SAM 1/2 task of segmenting a single object per prompt with points, boxes or masks
image-level Matthews correlation coefficient of binary 'is the object present' prediction, in [-1, 1]
a learned global token that predicts p(NP is present in input) while each query only solves p(q_i is a match | NP present); final score is the product
MV accepts or rejects masks on quality and relevance to the NP; EV checks that all instances of the NP have been masked
a Llama 3.2 model fine-tuned on human MV or EV labels to do those tasks automatically
a spatial-temporal mask tracking one object through a video
sum over a window of +1/-1 depending on whether a masklet matches a detection with IoU above a threshold
phrase-based HOTA: each video-NP pair is remapped to a unique video id with a single category, then HOTA is computed class-agnostically
overlap divided by the area of the smaller mask, used to find nested instances and for counting NMS
a phrase absent from the image for which (a previous generation of) SAM 3 predicts masks, i.e. adversarial to SAM 3
a phrase not seen in the combined set of SA-Co/HQ, SA-Co/EXT and SA-Co/VIDEO
